title: Low-touch onboarding & cost calibration playbook for runtime integrations
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a low-touch onboarding flow and a repeatable cost-calibration process for new developer integrations that use the Redwood runtime (hosted, dedicated, or private). The goal is to let small teams onboard quickly with predictable economics, while giving Redwood tools the telemetry and knobs needed to recommend batching, caching, and fidelity settings when usage stabilizes.

Scope:
- Audience: product managers, solution engineers, developer advocates, and partner integrations teams.
- Applies to: new SaaS integrations, marketplace connectors, and developer sandboxes that consume text generation, embeddings, or chat endpoints.
- Out of scope: large enterprise Dedicated contracts (handled by the Dedicated onboarding playbook) and air-gapped on-prem installations.

Goals:
1. Allow self-serve onboarding within 1 day for prototype integrations.
2. Produce a calibrated cost profile within 2 weeks of steady usage.
3. Surface automated recommendations (batching, quantization profile, KV cache TTL) with expected cost delta and latency impact.
4. Keep manual operations to a minimum unless a customer requests enterprise assistance.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Low-touch: minimal manual intervention from Redwood SRE/product teams; relies on SDKs, templates, and auto-telemetry.
- Calibrated cost profile: an expected per-1k-token cost range and latency distribution derived from observed traffic and model variant usage.
- Stabilization window: 14 consecutive days where per-route token variance is within ±25%.

Quickstart onboarding flow (1–7 days):
1) Self-serve sign-up and sample app
   - Developer signs up and receives starter credits.
   - SDK quickstart template (Node/Python) with preconfigured client, example prompts, and a local simulator.
2) Integrate in sandbox mode
   - Use the "dev-sandbox" runtime route (pre-provisioned warm capacity).
   - Enable telemetry flag: enable_cost_capture: true.
3) Smoke test and synthetic traffic
   - Run the packaged synthetic runner (./tools/synthetic-runner) for 1–2 hours to validate latency and token accounting.
4) Promote to low-traffic production (soft launch)
   - Flip route to "soft-prod" with a 1 rps cap for first 48 hours.
5) Automated analysis and initial recommendations (48–72 hours)
   - The Optimize assistant ingests telemetry and returns: batching suggestion, cache TTL, model variant suggestion, and projected cost impact.
6) Accept recommendations or schedule a calibration review with an SRE (optional)
7) Enter stabilization and cost calibration window (up to 14 days)

Cost calibration procedure (2–14 days):
- Objective: map observed traffic patterns to an operational cost model and produce a recommended configuration.
- Inputs: 14-day traffic sample, token length distribution, interactive vs batch ratios, session affinity, and KV cache hit-rate.
- Outputs: per-route cost projection, recommended batching and cache settings, suggested model quantization tier (if available), and expected latency delta.

Calibration runbook (step-by-step):
1. Pull telemetry snapshot:
   - Query: SELECT route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, kv_cache_hits, requests FROM runtime_telemetry WHERE route = '<route>' AND timestamp BETWEEN now() - interval '14 days' AND now();
2. Compute token distribution and session patterns.
3. Run cost simulation model using the Optimize SDK:
   - simulate_cost(traffic_sample, candidate_configs) -> ranked suggestions.
4. Review top-3 suggestions and their tradeoffs.
5. Apply a single recommendation as A/B (10% traffic canary) or apply globally for low-volume routes.
6. Re-measure over 48–72 hours and iterate until stabilization window achieved.

Recommended thresholds and SLOs for low-touch cohort:
| Metric | Target (low-touch) | Escalation threshold | Rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| P50 token gen latency | <= 100 ms | > 200 ms for 1 hour | Typical dev UX expectation |
| P95 token gen latency | <= 350 ms | > 700 ms for 15 min | Interactive sessions should remain responsive |
| KV cache hit-rate | >= 20% | < 5% sustained | Even small cache use reduces token cost |
| Cost variance | +/- 20% of projection | > +/- 40% | Signals mis-modeling or bursty traffic |

Recommended automated knobs (examples):
- Batching: target 8–32 concurrent in-flight tokens for non-interactive endpoints.
- KV cache TTL: 5–30 minutes depending on session stickiness.
- Quantization profile: recommend 4-bit quant for embeddings-heavy, 8-bit for high-fidelity chat.

Runtime configuration examples:
- Route-level YAML (example):

route: user-chat-low-touch
enabled: true
mode: soft-prod
model_preference:
  - name: redwood-gpt-large-quantized-8bit
    fallback: redwood-gpt-medium-quantized-4bit
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  target_batch_size: 16
cache:
  kv_cache_enabled: true
  ttl_seconds: 600
telemetry:
  enable_cost_capture: true
  sample_rate: 0.25

- CLI commands for SRE/developer:
  # Run local synthetic runner against route (2 concurrent workers)
  ./tools/synthetic-runner --route user-chat-low-touch --workers 2 --duration 3600

Automated recommendations payload (example):
{
  "route": "user-chat-low-touch",
  "recommendations": [
    {"type":"batching","target_batch_size":16,"expected_cost_delta":"-12%","expected_p95_latency_delta":"+30ms"},
    {"type":"kv_cache","ttl_seconds":600,"expected_cost_delta":"-8%","notes":"best for repeat Q/A"}
  ]
}

Rollout patterns and guardrails:
- Canary: 10% traffic for 48–72 hours with automatic rollback if P95 latency increases > 2x or error rate > 1%.
- A/B: 10/90 split for behavioral validation (cost vs quality).
- Full apply: only after 14-day calibration and no regression trends.

Success metrics (measured at route-level):
- Time to first successful soft-prod (days) < 1 day.
- Time to calibration (days) <= 14 days from soft-prod.
- Net cost delta after applying recommendations: target -10% to -30% without >25% P95 increase.
- Developer satisfaction (qualitative): integration rating >= 4/5 in post-onboarding survey.

Known limitations and escalation paths:
- Very bursty enterprise traffic (variance > 200%) should be escalated to Dedicated onboarding.
- High-safety or regulated workloads requiring audit logs beyond default retention must use Private onboarding.
- If automated calibration repeatedly fails (3 attempts) escalate to Solutions Engineering with telemetry bundle.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Product (onboarding playbook): maintain templates and UX.
- Developer DX: SDKs, quickstarts, synthetic runner maintenance.
- Optimize team: cost simulation model and recommendations API.
- SRE escalation: handle canary rollbacks and infra incidents.

Appendix A — quick checklist for Solutions Engineers (for low-touch cases):
- Verify telemetry flags enabled.
- Run synthetic runner and validate p50/p95.
- Confirm default batching and cache settings applied.
- Review Optimize recommendations and record decision in ticket.

Appendix B — example ticket template (copy-paste into ticketing tool):
Title: Calibrate route <route> after soft-prod
Description:
- Route: <route>
- Traffic start: <iso-date>
- Synthetic runner artifacts: <links>
- Recommendation applied: <yes/no>
- Next review date: <iso-date>
